correctness.rationale: For odd dimension 2m+1 the geodesic integration weight is sin^(2m)(theta). The cosine expansion of the weighted Gegenbauer polynomial is supported on n,n+2,...,n+2m by polynomial degree, parity, and orthogonality. Vanishing through derivative order 2m−1 at zero cancels the first m large-a terms in the rational combination of the cosine transforms; after a[1−(−1)^n exp(−pi a)] is factored out, the numerator over the product denominator is constant. The local coefficient C_n^(m)(1) at theta^(2m) fixes that constant to (2m)! C_n^(m)(1). This includes n=0 with its a² denominator factor. The affine correction multiplies the positive transform by 1−bR, with R its logarithmic a derivative. R increases strictly in each parity; the even limit is the larger and is unattained. The difference R_1−R_0 is strictly positive because its first rational term 2/[a(a²+1)] exceeds pi/sinh(pi a), as seen using the cubic Taylor lower bound for sinh. Thus the minimum is R_0<0, and the two reciprocal thresholds are necessary and sufficient. Only degree zero disappears at the lower boundary; at the upper boundary all degrees remain positive and the even coefficients have an extra asymptotic factor 2aU(m+1)/n². The two-parity strictness criterion holds at both boundaries. The coth expansion or the partial fraction series gives R_0=−pi/2+a/(2m)+O_a(m^-2), so L_m increases to −2/pi with the stated correction. Equatorial embedding gives the all-sphere intersection, not a separate sharp interval for each even dimension. Random hemisphere signs supply the stated geometric check.
